REVIEW 195e83f20c24c47b49f73f2062e957865623bb90 (CorpusReader refusal cap, bd-01M37D6APTEQTVVSMSC195Z184): APPROVE. No BLOCK. Independent reviewer: claude-release, not the proposer. Ancestry: 70358e4e is an ancestor (8aace81e, 5c4c5862, 195e83f2).
Source: openRows emits refusals in the old row-then-binding-column order, counts every one (seen), keeps the first RefusalCap, and returns every row. No per-row or sheet-wide refusal vector remains. The doc now says "retains" rather than "collects", which is accurate.
Independent run, fresh --shared clone at the exact SHA, fatal warnings, corpusIntake/testOnly CorpusReaderSuite: 24/0.
- Mutant C1 (cap off by one, <): killed by "a many-error sheet keeps the first 100 refusals...".
- Mutant C2 (count only the kept refusals): killed by the same test (260 total).
- Source restored, tree clean. Logs: ~/.claude/jobs/48a9214c/tmp/cr-*.log.
FOLLOW-UP (a nit): the court checks the column SET {B, C}, not the within-row order (B before C). A binding-order regression would pass. Asserting sheet.refusals.take(2).map(_.coordinate.column) == Vector("B", "C") would pin it.
